hints: Look at what those two IR numbers are telling you, each wavenumber points to a specific bond in the molecule.
A broad absorption near 3400 cm-1 means an O-H group, so rule out any isomer that has oxygen but no O-H.
Now just count how many different carbon skeletons can hold that OH group for formula C4H10O, remember straight chains and branched chains.
walkthrough:
**Decode the IR data**

Think like a detective. IR peaks tell you which bonds are present.

Absorption at $3400 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ = O-H stretch (broad, hydrogen-bonded alcohol or phenol). Absorption at $1200 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ = C-O stretch.

**Decide the functional group**

With formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, we have only two possibilities for oxygen: alcohol ($\text{C-O-H}$) or ether ($\text{C-O-C}$).

Ethers have C-O but no O-H, so they would NOT absorb at 3400 cm-1. Only alcohols give BOTH peaks.

**Count the alcohol structural isomers**

Now count every distinct way to arrange 4 carbons with an -OH group.

Straight chain C4: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (butan-1-ol) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ (butan-2-ol). That is 2 isomers.

**Add the branched isomers**

Branched skeleton is 2-methylpropane.

$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ (2-methylpropan-1-ol) and $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$ (2-methylpropan-2-ol). That is 2 more isomers.

Total = 2 + 2 = 4 isomers.

options.A: 2 counts only half the alcohols, usually just butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol. It forgets the branched skeleton based on 2-methylpropane which gives two more distinct alcohols.
options.B: 4 is correct. Only alcohols show both O-H (3400 cm-1) and C-O (1200 cm-1). There are exactly 4 structural alcohol isomers of C4H10O: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
options.C: 6 is too high. It may come from counting ether isomers as well, or from double counting positions of OH that are identical by symmetry. Ethers do not absorb at 3400 cm-1 so they must be excluded.
options.D: 7 is the total number of structural isomers of C4H10O (4 alcohols + 3 ethers). The question asks only for those with BOTH absorptions, so the 3 ethers (methoxypropanes and ethoxyethane) do not count.
